text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - node/rg-worker-12 ephemeral-storage pressure 95% -> eviction risk. pods in ns=serve showing Terminating/ContainerFailed; increased restart count for runtime-servex. Auto-escalation to oncall alice (pager) at 06:02 UTC.

alice (oncall): seeing it, joining. can someone post quick impact?

carla (sre): metrics: node FS used 98% now, kubelet eviction threshold triggered on /var/lib/kubelet/plugins and /var/lib/docker. eviction events: 
```
Aug 12 06:00:11 kubelet[1234]: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
Aug 12 06:00:12 kubelet[1234]: Unable to delete pod logs: remove /var/log/pods/...: no space left on device
```

carla (sre): several serve-runtime pods went CrashLoopBackOff; containerExitCode=137 somewhere (OOMKILL) but most are actually terminated by node eviction.

ben (runtime): logs show model-cache writes + debug logs spiking from a job that started at 05:48. write throughput high, temp writes to emptyDir /tmp/modelcache (ephemeral). stacktrace snippets: 
```
I 05:49:02 modelcache: wrote shard 12 size=3.6GB
W 05:50:10 logger debug flood: request_id=... payload_size=1.2MB
```

ben (runtime): also seeing CUDA driver messages on some restarts but those are after pod restarts. primary root looks like disk pressure from large epoch-run + verbose logging.

dan (eng-infra): checked node: `df -h` shows /var filled. `kubectl describe node rg-worker-12` shows eviction signals. I can cordon the node and drain safely if needed. recommend cordon then run urgent log cleanup then uncordon.

alice (oncall): cordon and drain? any risk to capacity? how many pods will move?

carla (sre): capacity risk low, we have spare nodes in cluster pool. but we should avoid mass simultaneous restarts of GPU-serving pods. set `maxUnavailable=1` for deployments temporarily.

ben (runtime): can we scale down the debug job that is spamming logs? job name `training-smoke-debugger`. I'm going to kill that job pod.

alice (oncall): ben go for it. dan you can cordon once ben stops the job.

ben (runtime): killed pod `training-smoke-debugger-7f8` - logs stopped spiking.

carla (sre): running a quick prune on node to free logs: 
```
sudo find /var/log/pods -mtime +3 -type f -delete --dry-run
# verified candidates (~12GB)
sudo find /var/log/pods -mtime +3 -type f -delete
```

carla (sre): freed ~18GB. /var usage dropped to 70%. pods are still being restarted because kubelet had marked some as Terminated. I'll restart kubelet on rg-worker-12 to clear stuck state.

dan (eng-infra): cordoning rg-worker-12 now: `kubectl cordon rg-worker-12` -> Ready scheduling disabled.

dan (eng-infra): starting `kubectl drain rg-worker-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m` to migrate pods. note: will cause restarts for the gpu-serving pods but they should schedule to other nodes.

frank (product): alert from monitoring says ~1.7% 5xx for hosted API during the window, spike lasted ~4m. any customer-facing incidents we should note?

eve (cust-success): I'm on watch. no high-rev customers complaining yet; alerting a couple of customers that saw transient failed requests. will prepare status blurb if we have ETA for full recovery.

ben (runtime): after drain some pods re-scheduled, but a few runtime-servex pods failed with `/bin/sh: write/append: no space left on device` in init container where we unpack cached models to emptyDir. those pods had restartCount 4 before coming back up.

carla (sre): that's because some pods use hostPath or large emptyDir size ephemeral. we need to ensure eviction-safe model-cache config for ephemeral volumes. immediate fix: set `emptyDir.medium: Memory` not possible for large shards. short term: add a cleanup job to delete old model shards older than N days from emptyDir cache dir on nodes.

alice (oncall): dan, can infra run a one-off cleanup daemonset to sweep /var/tmp/modelcache/*.older-than-48h ?

dan (eng-infra): yes. creating a privileged DaemonSet with tolerations to run a cleanup script. applying now. command snippet: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-ephemeral-cleanup
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cleaner
        image: alpine
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","find /var/tmp/modelcache -type f -mtime +2 -delete || true; sleep 3600"]
      hostPID: true
      hostNetwork: true
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 0
EOF
```

carla (sre): cleaner is running. observed additional ~10GB reclaimed on other nodes. overall cluster /var usage now at ~62%.

ben (runtime): I pushed a temporary change to reduce verbose logging on modelcache: `LOG_LEVEL=info` for the deployment `model-cache-writer`. also adjusted liveness probe to allow longer startup while caches warm up.

alice (oncall): good. are customer requests recovery trending back to normal? frank?

frank (product): 5xx back down to baseline ~0.2% within 8 minutes of cleanup. good recovery.

eve (cust-success): sending short notification: "Transient increased errors for a subset of hosted API requests between 06:00-06:10 UTC due to node storage pressure. Services recovered after cleanup and pod rescheduling. No data loss reported." will send after you approve.

carla (sre): follow-ups to prevent recurrence: 
- ensure per-pod ephemeral-storage requests/limits set for model-cache and runtime pods
- convert log rotation to compress + rotate hourly for high-volume components
- create a guardrail in autoscaler to avoid scheduling large ephemeral-write jobs onto worker nodes with <20% free ephemeral space
- replace long-lived debug job with sandboxed bucket writes (S3) not local ephemeral

dan (eng-infra): opening infra ticket INF-4207 to add eviction-aware scheduler predicate and node-level cleanup cron.

ben (runtime): I'll add a model-cache config to respect `TMPDIR` override to use a mounted PVC for large shards in Dedicated clusters. PR incoming.

alice (oncall): handing off to carla for postmortem. my shift ends in 25. Tags: :white_check_mark: incident mitigated.

carla (sre): taking postmortem lead. will gather logs, ETA for hardening and follow-ups. will include timelines and customer list.

alice (oncall): passing pager to dan (infra oncall) for the next 12h watch. thanks all. :thumbsup:

dan (eng-infra): ack -- I'll monitor the cleaner and node pool.

eve (cust-success): sending approved blurb now.

frank (product): thumbs up. let's add this to monthly reliability notes.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident auto-close timer set to 72h; mark resolved when follow-ups are tracked.

carla (sre): assigned to follow-ups: INF-4207, RUNTIME-778 (model-cache tmpdir), LOG-301 (rotate/compress). scheduling postmortem doc."
